note: Every gate in the estate, in one registry, with the one fact that decides where it may run: whether it needs a network. The ordering rule is that offline gates run first, on the machine, and nothing that touches the network or publishes anything runs until they have all passed.
why: Written 202609050325 after a live fault that no gate could have caught: the MAP button in Pipeline News pointed at a receiver carrying no engine. The page served, so nothing 404'd and no monitor complained. A gate that only asks whether a URL answers cannot see that. The estate needs one place that knows what is checked, what is not, and which checks can be trusted when the network is what has changed.
ordering: 1. offline — run on the machine, no socket. If any fails, stop.
3. publish — only after 2. Nothing here publishes.

checkout_note: Which clone a gate reads is declared here, not guessed. Default is the declared path and only that. A repo with sibling clones that differ declares a search with the branch that decides it, and lib/checkout.mjs fails loudly on zero matches or more than one rather than falling back to whatever readdirSync returned first — the fault that made menu-map.mjs give exit 0 and exit 1 twenty minutes apart with nothing changed on disk.
required_note: Every gate is required unless it says "required": false. A required gate whose clone is absent BLOCKS the run and the exit code: absence is not a pass and it is not neutral either.
